subject: Solstice AI: connectivity blueprint kickoff
messages:
From: Alan Kumar <alan.kumar@solstice.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Solstice AI — connectivity & on-prem blueprint kickoff

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. We're ready to kick off the private deployment workstream for Solstice AI. Scope for this engagement: VPC peering into our AWS account, private endpoints for model traffic, and the on-prem appliance packaging for our staging datacenter.

High-level asks:  
- Confirm expected CIDR ranges (we can share ours) and whether Redwood prefers using Transit Gateway or direct peering for the initial rollout.
- Guidance on private endpoint lifecycle (DNS, certificates, health checks).
- On-prem artifact format and installer expectations (we will have a hardened host image and a K8s cluster option).

I've attached our initial network blueprint and an install manifest. Sophie (cc) will be our operations lead. Can we get an initial 60-minute technical kickoff this week? Our team is available Thu/Fri morning PST.

Attachments: solstice_network_blueprint_v1.pdf, onprem_install_manifest_v2.xlsx

Thanks,
Alan Kumar
Head of Infrastructure, Solstice AI
alan.kumar@solstice.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alan Kumar <alan.kumar@solstice.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@solstice.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solstice AI — connectivity & on-prem blueprint kickoff

Hi Alan — thanks, appreciate the materials. Happy to run the kickoff. Proposed plan and immediate asks below so we come prepared:  

1) Kickoff agenda (60m)
- Introductions and success criteria (10m)
- Network topology review (Transit GW vs peering) (15m)
- Private endpoint and DNS model (10m)
- On-prem package delivery & installer UX (10m)
- Rollout cadence, canary, and rollback plan (10m)

2) Pre-kickoff artifacts we need from your side (please send prior to meeting):
- CIDR blocks and existing VPC layout (list of subnets, AZs)
- Desired egress / NAT plan and any firewall appliance IPs
- KMS/HSM vendor details if using customer-managed keys for inference traffic
- A small sample of the installer (tarball) or a manifest describing required ports and systemd services

3) Action owners from Redwood: Marcus will lead VPC peering design and firewall rules; Laura will lead on-prem installation acceptance and installer validation. I'll own the rollout and post-install validation checklist.

We can do Thu 16 May 2029 at 09:30 PST — does that work for you? If so, I'll send a calendar invite and a shared pre-kickoff checklist (confluence + checklist).

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Alan Kumar <alan.kumar@solstice.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 12:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solstice AI — connectivity & on-prem blueprint kickoff

Irene / Alan — quick note from the infra perspective:  

- For the initial phase I'd prefer Transit Gateway if Solstice is expecting multi-VPC traffic patterns (ingress from multiple accounts). If it's a single consumer VPC and you want lower operational overhead, direct VPC peering is fine.
- Please confirm whether you'll need cross-account IAM roles for Redwood to push route table updates, or if we'll hand you a route configuration to apply.
- Also need the expected p95 packet size and peak sustained connections; that helps size NIC and MTU checks on the appliance.

I'll prepare a candidate security group + NACL template and share it ahead of the kickoff.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Cloud Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Alan Kumar <alan.kumar@solstice.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@solstice.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solstice AI — connectivity & on-prem blueprint kickoff

Thanks — Thu 16 May 09:30 PST works for us. Per Marcus' questions, attaching the VPC/exported topology and a CSV of the IP ranges we plan to use. A few specifics:  

- We're single-account for now but expect to onboard two more internal accounts in Q3. Given that, Transit Gateway sounds reasonable as a longer-term path but we can start with peering if that shortens the timeline.
- We'll allow a cross-account role for Redwood to apply route updates (role ARN included in attached CSV as a note).
- p95 packet size for our model traffic is ~1.2KB; peak sustained simultaneous connections to the endpoint can hit ~1.8k during load tests.

Attachments: vpc_peering_ip_ranges.csv (contains CIDRs and role ARNs), solstice_network_blueprint_v1.pdf (updated)

Looking forward — Sophie and I will be on the call.

—Alan

Subject: Re: Solstice AI — connectivity & on-prem blueprint kickoff

Alan / Sophie — thanks for the updated artifacts, received and reviewed. Next steps before the Thu kickoff:  

1) Preflight checklist (we completed the following items on our side):
- Marcus uploaded a candidate security group + NACL template to the shared drive.
- Laura validated the installer manifest fields against Redwood's acceptance schema; two minor items flagged (TLS fingerprint metadata, and a post-install healthcheck endpoint).

2) Items for Solstice to confirm (please send before 16 May 06:00 PST):
- Final CIDR list (we have the CSV but need confirmation of the /28 reserved for the management interface)
- KMS key policy snippet for cross-account usage (if using customer-managed keys)
- Any on-prem firewall egress rules blocking outbound 443/853 (DNS over TLS) to the Redwood control plane

3) Call invite: I've scheduled the kickoff Thu, 16 May 2029 09:30–10:30 PST (Calendar invite sent). Meeting link and pre-kickoff Confluence are in the invite.  

4) Rollout proposal (high level) — for discussion on Thu:
- Phase 0: Preflight & peering test (staging VPC peering, smoke tests)
- Phase 1: Private endpoint + DNS cutover (small percentage of traffic)
- Phase 2: On-prem appliance install (staged canary hosts)
- Phase 3: Scale and monitor (traffic shift + automatic fallback)

I'll bring the rollout checklist and a short validation harness (artifact) to the call. If any blockers arise, flag them by replying to this thread and I'll escalate.

Best,
Irene
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
